title: Number Classifier
story: Your math teacher assigns 50 numbers and asks you to label each as positive, negative, or zero — and then check which ones are even and divisible by 3. Doing this by hand would take an hour. Three small functions can finish it in seconds.
why: A suite of number-classifying functions shows how Boolean and String-returning functions can answer different questions about the same data — each function is a specialized lens.
analogy: These functions are like different tools in a toolbox. `classify()` is the label maker — it puts a sticker on each number. `is_even()` is a two-hole punch — it checks if the number fits. `is_divisible_by()` is an adjustable wrench — you set the divisor and it tells you if the fit is perfect.
try_it: Add a fourth function `is_odd(n: Int) -> Bool` that reuses `is_even` (hint: return !is_even(n)). Then write a `describe_number(n: Int) -> Str` function that combines classify, is_even, and is_divisible_by into one descriptive sentence.
tips: classify uses a three-way if/elif/else: positive, negative, and zero are the only possibilities
is_even is a one-liner: a number is even when n % 2 == 0
is_divisible_by protects against division by zero — always check d == 0 first
Each function has one clear question in its name — if you can't name it, split it
common_mistakes: Writing `if n > 0` then `else if n < 0` instead of `elif n < 0` — use elif for chained conditions
Forgetting the zero case in classify — every Int falls into one of three buckets
Returning 0 or 1 instead of true/false from Boolean functions
Not checking d == 0 in is_divisible_by — modulo by zero crashes the program
